name: Vail Or Veil
overview: The Scripture presents the vail or veil primarily as a physical and symbolic covering, often worn by women as a token of modesty and subjection, as seen when Rebekah covered herself upon meeting Isaac's servant (Genesis 24:65) and Tamar wrapped herself in a veil (Genesis 38:14). Moses used a veil to conceal the glory of his face after speaking with God (Exodus 34:33), illustrating the veil's role in hiding divine radiance. Furthermore, the veil symbolizes spiritual blindness, both of the Gentile nations and the Jewish people, as described in Isaiah 25:7. The removal of the veil is portrayed as a form of dishonor or punishment, exemplified by the watchmen taking the veil from the woman in Song of Solomon 5:7, emphasizing the cultural and spiritual significance of this covering.
